places.text: The South Luangwa has one of the densest leopard populations in Africa, and the best chance of seeing one hunting.
places.title: Leopard Country

places.text: Invented in the Luangwa in the 1950s: no vehicle, an armed scout, and everything at eye level.
places.title: The Walking Safari

places.text: The old colonial capital above the falls, its museum, and the tree where the man himself is said to have camped.
places.title: Livingstone

places.text: World Heritage since 1989, shared with Zimbabwe, and named by the Kololo long before anyone renamed it.
places.title: Mosi-oa-Tunya, UNESCO

places.text: The centre of everything: Kabwata market, the Great East Road, and the flights that get you to the parks.
places.title: Lusaka

places.text: Corrugated iron and deep colonial verandas along Mosi-oa-Tunya Road, built for heat and never modernised.
places.title: Livingstone's Verandas

places.text: Escarpment, floodplain and winterthorn forest, with the river braiding through the middle of all of it.
places.title: The Zambezi Valley

places.text: Two thousand metres of rolling montane grassland on the Malawi border, with roan antelope and no heat.
places.title: The Nyika Plateau

places.text: Victoria Falls needs no introduction; Kalambo, on the Tanzanian border, drops 235 metres in a single uninterrupted fall.
places.title: Victoria and Kalambo

places.text: Three great river systems and the southern tip of Lake Tanganyika, the second deepest lake on earth.
places.title: Zambezi, Kafue, Tanganyika

places.text: Clear freshwater, sand and forested hills at Nsumbu, about as far from anywhere as Zambia gets.
places.title: Lake Tanganyika Shore

places.text: Miombo woodland turning red at the start of the rains, and the winterthorn groves the elephants feed under.
places.title: Miombo and Winterthorn

places.text: Swim to the lip of Victoria Falls in low water, then raft the grade five rapids in the Batoka gorge below it.
places.title: Devil's Pool and the Gorge

places.text: Seventy-three ethnic groups, seven official languages, and a royal barge ceremony older than the country.
places.title: Lozi, Bemba, Tonga

places.text: The Lozi live with the flood — moving cattle, homes and the king himself when the Zambezi rises.
places.title: The Barotse Floodplain

places.text: Maize nshima with relish, dried kapenta from the lakes, and fresh bream out of the Zambezi.
places.title: Nshima and Kapenta

places.text: When the floodplain fills, the Litunga is paddled to high ground on the Nalikwanda barge, drummed the whole way.
places.title: Kuomboka

places.text: Tight coiled baskets from the Western Province, and copper worked on the belt that built the economy.
places.title: Basketry and Copper

places.text: Roadside charcoal and tomatoes, long-haul trucks to the copperbelt, and a bus that leaves when it fills.
places.title: Markets and the Great North Road

places.text: Community campsites and craft cooperatives on the Luangwa boundary, funded by the same beds that fill the lodges.
places.title: Village Around the Park

places.text: Three days downstream past hippo pods and elephant crossings, camping on islands, no engine at any point.
places.title: Canoeing the Lower Zambezi

places.text: Seasonal bush camps in the Luangwa that take six guests, close at the rains, and are walked between.
places.title: Bush Camps, Six Beds

places.text: Kafue is the size of Wales; the conservation programmes there fund anti-poaching across the whole Greater Kafue system.
places.title: Kafue and the Carnivores

places.text: The river bends, the hippo surface and the dust goes gold about forty minutes before the drive has to end.
places.title: Luangwa at Last Light

places.text: The second largest wildebeest migration in Africa, on a plain almost nobody has heard of, reachable only in the dry.
places.title: Liuwa Plain

places.text: Zambia kept the walking safari, the small camp and the empty park while its neighbours scaled up.
places.title: Wilderness, Still Unmanaged
